text:
Maria (CS): FYI Sentinel just flagged a hard 429/TP SLO breach during a marketing blast. Happened ~2026-04-12 10:15 UTC. Customer says burst credits were '0' and requests were dropped. Logs attached by customer (see IDs).
Tom (oncall): thanks—can you paste a sample request_id and the timestamp range?
Maria (CS): request_ids: rq_8f3a2, rq_8f3a5, rq_8f3b0. Spike window ~10:14:30–10:17:00 UTC. Customer sent ~1.2M tokens in 3m. They were on Dedicated pool "sentinel-prod-usw2".
Ella (Infra): looking at infra metrics now. I see tokens/s spike to ~14k at 10:15. The configured headroom for that pool is 7k T/s and burst_credits were at 0 by the time we started dropping. Autoscaler did attempt a scale but cooldown prevented full capacity add—we hit instance quota in the region.
Li (SRE): admission control logs show immediate rejects at the peak. snippet: 
```
[admission] 2026-04-12T10:15:18Z reject token 14230 reason=burst_exhausted pool=sentinel-prod-usw2
```
Also seeing long-running 1k+ seq requests from another tenant (id: tenant-peak) that kept GPU KV cache warm for long sequences — noisy neighbor behavior.
Tom (oncall): can you share the admission_control config for that pool? want to see burst policy + headroom settings.
Ella (Infra): paste of current policy: 
```
admission_control:
  headroom_tps: 7000
  burst_credits_per_pool: 10000
  token_cost_model: per_token
  eviction_policy: graceful
  scale_cooldown_s: 300
```
Tom (oncall): weird — burst_credits_per_pool 10k should've helped, but they hit 1.2M tokens in 3m (~6667 T/s average) with peaks far above that. Looks like credits were consumed within first minute. Also scale_cooldown 300s prevented the autoscaler from adding more nodes quickly.
Li (SRE): noisy neighbor exacerbated it — the long sequences prevented efficient batching and caused GPU saturation. When that tenant was creating long KV chains, effective throughput for short requests dropped and admission control consumed burst credits trying to smooth.
Maria (CS): customer asked if this is a billing issue or a capacity config problem. They want immediate remediation and a postmortem.
Jordan (AM): I'm looping in to manage customer comms. Quick action: offer temporary burst top-up & prioritize their queue while we investigate. I'll prepare a credit offer.
Ella (Infra): short-term mitigation steps I recommend now:
- bump headroom_tps to 12k for sentinel-prod-usw2
- set scale_cooldown_s to 60 for 30 minutes
- temporarily change eviction_policy to immediate for noisy tenant
I'll apply as a one-off and monitor.
Tom (oncall): do it and post the commands. Also let's capture metric screenshot and admission logs for the PM.
Ella (Infra): applying now. Commands used: 
```bash
rdwctl pools update sentinel-prod-usw2 --headroom-tps 12000 \
  --burst-credits 20000 --scale-cooldown 60
rdwctl tenant update tenant-peak --eviction-policy immediate
```
deploy-bot: Deployment started for pool config update (change-id: cfg-2293).
Ella (Infra): changes applied at 10:37 UTC. Monitoring shows drops stopped within ~45s and tokens/s back to ~6k baseline. Burst credits now at ~18000 post-topup.
Li (SRE): for the long term: recommend:
- raise pool reserve headroom to 1.5x expected daily peak for customers running marketing blasts (set template to 1.5 * 95th percentile)
- implement per-tenant long-seq detection that triggers soft throttles before global burst exhaustion
- add quota alerts when burst_credits < 20% and autoscaler cannot scale due to region quota
- consider automatic temporary pinning to extra nodes for tenants flagged as "blast" in schedule.
Tom (oncall): agree. Also add a preflight check for big scheduled blasts (CS/AM should notify infra 24h prior). We can auto-suggest headroom bump.
Jordan (AM): I'll update our onboarding docs and offer a playbook to customers: expected token budget for campaigns, preflight checklist, and emergency contact.
Maria (CS): customer is happy with the immediate fix and wants a write-up. They asked for steps to reproduce if we need to run their blast in our staging.
Li (SRE): repro steps we used:
1) replay customer request stream in staging with same token distribution (script attached).
2) run a concurrent long-seq generator to emulate noisy neighbor: 
```bash
./seq-flood --tenant noisy --rps 50 --seq-len 1200
./replay_requests --input sentinel_replay.json --rps 200
```
3) observe admission metrics: `rdwctl metrics pool tokens_per_sec admission.rejects`
We reproduced rejection pattern and burst depletion within 90s.
Ella (Infra): follow-ups assigned:
- Li: design per-tenant long-seq detector (P0 for next sprint)
- Infra: change default pool template to 1.5x headroom for "marketing" tag (ops runbook)
- CS/AM: add preflight campaign notice to runbook (Jordan/Maria)
- SRE: add alert for burst_credit < 20% when autoscaler is in cooldown (Li/Tom)
Jordan (AM): I'll coordinate customer comms and send contract amendment options for reserved headroom if they want predictable behavior.
Maria (CS): nice work. I'll send the customer a timeline and the paste of the mitigation commands. Adding short postmortem doc and will link it here when ready. :thumbsup:
Tom (oncall): closing loop — we should add this thread to the postmortem. tagging for tracking: #incident-1798502468
deploy-bot: Config change cfg-2293 completed at 2026-04-12T10:37:45Z.
Li (SRE): last note — recommend we limit maximum per-request seq length by default or add quota-based penalties. Otherwise one tenant can degrade many others.
Maria (CS): acknowledged. We'll include that in the PM recommendations.
Jordan (AM): thanks team — I'll follow up with customer tomorrow with a summary and options.
Tom (oncall): marking as resolved for now. Will reopen if we see recurrences.
